draft.title: Random and non-random sampling
card: every member of the population has an equal chance of being picked, such as drawing names from a hat.
some members are more likely to be picked than others, such as asking only your friends or only people who volunteer.
Non-random samples can be biased. Bias means the results lean one way and do not fairly show the whole population.
Example: to find the favourite sport of a school of 800, picking 40 names by random draw is fair. Asking only the football team is not, because it leaves out most students.
draft.remember: Equal chances give a random sample. Unequal chances can make the results biased.

a.q: A school in Ballarat has 600 students. Which way of choosing 30 of them gives a random sample?
opts: Drawing 30 names from a box with all 600 names in it
Asking the first 30 students to walk in the school gate
Asking 30 students from the choir at their lunch practice
Asking 30 students who put their hand up at assembly
a.why: Only the name draw gives each of the 600 students the same chance of being picked. Asking the first to arrive is tempting, but early arrivals are a particular group, so students who come later have less chance. Choir members and volunteers are particular groups too.
a.clue: In which method does each student have the same chance?

b.q: Priya wants to know how often people in her Geelong suburb use the library. She surveys people as they leave it. Why are her results likely to be biased?
opts: Library users are more likely to be picked than others
People who rarely visit are more likely to be picked
Everyone in the suburb has the same chance of being picked
Random samples tend to give more biased results
b.why: Only people at the library can be picked, so frequent users have a much greater chance and the results will lean towards them. It is tempting to reverse this, but people who rarely visit are the ones least likely to be at the door.
b.clue: Who could never be picked at the library door?

a.best: Drawing 30 names from a box with all 600 names in it

b.best: Library users are more likely to be picked than others
